reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows higher GAAP net revenues, operating income, pretax income and parent-attributable net income, with operating expenses roughly flat, so the sequential operating margin widened on the displayed rows. The company-defined adjusted parent measure also rose, but by less than the GAAP parent figure, so the two bases diverge and the adjusted measure should not be read as a cleaner version of the GAAP result. Revenue growth is not attributable to organic client demand: average and ending AUM rose while net cash flows remained negative, and the AUM bridge is dominated by market appreciation, which itself was smaller than in the prior quarter. The effective fee rate excluding performance fees declined slightly, so revenue growth is consistent with a larger asset base rather than a richer fee take. A swing in capital allocation-based income, a signed and volatile line, contributed to the revenue change and is not evidence of a durable trend. The tax provision rose in line with higher pretax income, so the tax line is not a source of the profit improvement and must not be described as a reduced tax drag. Performance-based advisory fees were unchanged, so they do not explain the revenue change. The Q3-only managed account model delivery addition is a company-reported AUM addition, not a net flow, and has no Q2 comparator, so it cannot be used to offset the negative net cash flow figure. All comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic, not year-over-year, and no causal driver is established by these rows. Because the evidence is a selected extract with no complete filing, no segment detail, no guidance-versus-realized reconciliation and no year-over-year comparator, the research state is maintained rather than upgraded; conviction and status are unchanged and no valuation or trade conclusion is drawn.
